memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then they made fifty gold clasps and used them to fasten the two sets of curtains together so that the tabernacle was a unit." - Exod 36:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Loops alone did not hold anything. Something had to pass through them and lock them together — fifty gold clasps.

Small objects. Expensive material. Completely hidden once the tabernacle stood. And without them, the whole covering fell apart.

That is a fair picture of what actually holds people together. Not programmes or events, but small, costly, largely invisible things — a forgiveness nobody heard about, a difficult conversation handled gently, a person who chose to stay when leaving would have been easier.

Paul names the clasp directly: over all these virtues put on love, which binds them all together in perfect unity (Col 3:14). Love is what passes through the loops.

Notice the material. Gold — the most valuable substance they had — used for something no one would ever see. God does not reserve the precious things for display.

And the purpose is stated plainly: "so that the tabernacle was a unit." Not a collection of curtains. One dwelling place for God.

Christ Himself is the ultimate clasp. In Him all things hold together (Col 1:17), and He is our peace, who has made the two groups one and destroyed the barrier (Eph 2:14).

What is God asking you to invest in a relationship that no one will notice?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What hidden, costly thing is holding a relationship in your life together?
2. Are you willing to spend something precious where no one will see it?
3. How does Christ hold your life together?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You hold all things together. Make love the clasp in every relationship You have given me. Amen.
